title: Our Favorite Merino Wool Socks Are on Sale
gist: Wired's Scott Gilbertson promotes a sale on Darn Tough merino wool socks ($25 to $18 at REI), citing merino's anti-microbial and thermoregulating properties and a lifetime warranty he says he tested.

insights.claim: Darn Tough merino socks are discounted 28 percent, from $25 to $18 at REI, in an affiliate-linked Wired deal post.
insights.speaker: Scott Gilbertson
insights.so_what: Promotional price datapoint; no market signal beyond consumer deal flow.

insights.claim: The author argues merino's anti-microbial, sweat-wicking and thermoregulating properties make a higher merino percentage better for socks.
insights.speaker: Scott Gilbertson
insights.so_what: Material-quality claim underpinning premium sock pricing.
insights.quote: Merino wool is anti-microbial, meaning your socks don't smell at the end of the day.

insights.claim: The author says a lifetime warranty is credible because his own pairs have lasted over five years without holes and his wife's worn pair was replaced no questions asked.
insights.speaker: Scott Gilbertson
insights.so_what: A durable-goods warranty acts as a marketing moat, but evidence here is anecdotal.
insights.quote: The warranty is real, and WIRED-tested.
